subject: Commercial: tiered runtime bundling and pilot exit credits for TideHealth
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@tidehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@tidehealth.com
Date: 2027-03-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial: tiered runtime bundling and pilot exit credits for TideHealth

Hi Logan / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick econ check internally and have two asks before we decide on vendor replacement. Short version: can Redwood get within ~10% of the incumbent's run-rate and give a low-friction pilot exit credit to cover migration effort?

Details:
- Current vendor: CloudForge (we're mid-contract, run-rate ~ $38k/mo for inference + embeddings).
- Primary asks: price alignment for first 12 months, and a pilot exit credit covering egress + engineering time if we choose to revert within 90 days.
- We also need clarity on packaging: do you recommend dedicated vs hosted for our workload (see baseline attached)?

Attached: tidehealth_prod_baseline.csv (rough 30-day usage sample).

Goal: get a short commercial term sheet we can share with procurement/legal this week. Can Redwood propose a practical packaging + credit structure and a timeline to sign?

Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
TideHealth
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@tidehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial: tiered runtime bundling and pilot exit credits for TideHealth

Samir — appreciate the baseline and the clarity. Laura and I discussed; we're aligned to propose a pragmatic two-part offer: a short pilot credit to de-risk migration + a tiered runtime bundle for year-one that narrows the run-rate gap.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Stephanie, can you confirm estimated onboarding effort and whether any of TideHealth's peak patterns require Dedicated capacity?
2) I'll draft a one-page term sheet (commercial points only) and attach a pilot credits matrix for your review.
3) If procurement/legal needs a DocuSign-ready side letter for egress/SLA protections, we can route that to our legal team — want to surface that early.

Samir — aiming to get a draft to you by EOD tomorrow. Is a Wednesday (2027-03-09) signature target realistic for you?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: pilot-credits-matrix.xlsx (working draft)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@tidehealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial: tiered runtime bundling and pilot exit credits for TideHealth

Samir / team — quick note from CS/Onboarding:

Review of the attached baseline shows a steady 95th percentile token throughput and occasional 2x spikes during nightly batch jobs. Here's our read:
- Hosted will likely meet your latency goals for the pilot and is lower ops lift.
- Dedicated is recommended if you want guaranteed tail-latency under heavy batch spikes (or if you need strict data isolation).

Onboarding estimate (conservative): 4–6 weeks for pilot (two-week smoke test, two-week integration, rolling production cutover). We can reduce to ~3 weeks with active TideHealth engineering involvement and temporary pairing for KV cache tuning.

Pilot credit structure suggestion (we can flex):
- Option A (low friction): 90-day pilot, up to $25k in credits to cover extra egress and runbooks if you choose to revert.
- Option B (deeper ramp): 3-month pilot + $15k onboarding credit + $15k revert credit, plus one week of embedded on-call for cutover.

We will also capture a usage baseline during the pilot to make the year-one bundling more accurate. If Laura/Logan want to be conservative commercially, we can propose a cap on seat-rate increases for 12 months.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@tidehealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial: tiered runtime bundling and pilot exit credits for TideHealth

Samir — thanks, this is helpful. Internal note: I have informal approval to offer the following commercial package as a compromise to get TideHealth across the finish line without setting an open precedent:

Proposed commercial bullets:
- Year-one tiered runtime bundle: 15% blended discount on token runtime for first 12 months, with a commitment to revisit after the pilot baseline is confirmed.
- Pilot de-risk package: 90-day pilot with a $25,000 revert/egress credit OR an alternative split ($15k onboarding + $15k revert) depending on which you prefer.
- Go-live support: one week of embedded on-call during cutover plus a 2-week accelerator window at no extra charge.
- Cap & protection: seat-rate cap for 12 months and an SLA carveout for the pilot period.

Attached is a draft one-pager proposal (proposal-draft-TideHealth.pdf) — Laura will route the language to Legal for a quick side-letter covering the egress/SLA ask.

Logan — if this looks right, send the non-binding term sheet to Samir and we'll follow up with Legal/Finance to finalize commercial and DocuSign routing.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposal-draft-TideHealth.pdf
From: Samir Patel <samir@tidehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-05T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial: tiered runtime bundling and pilot exit credits for TideHealth

Laura / Logan / Stephanie — appreciate the quick turnaround and concrete options. High level — this is workable. Two follow-ups before I share with procurement/legal:  

1) Can we get the egress/revert credit language as a one-paragraph side letter (DocuSign-ready)? We need explicit triggers (e.g., revert within 90 days after go-live; credit applied to last invoice).
2) For the year-one tier, will Redwood provide a usage true-up if actual baseline is materially different (>20%) from the pilot baseline?

If you can get those two items in writing, procurement is OK to proceed. Our target: signed non-binding term sheet by 2027-03-09 and DocuSign side letter in parallel.

Looking forward — Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
TideHealth
